investigations.name: recover-enzyme-kinetics
investigations.description:
Second rung. Ground truth is a Michaelis-Menten enzyme model; the synthetic
target exposes substrate and product trajectories (ES optionally hidden). This
rung forces a real modelling choice — elementary vs reduced rate law — so it is
where the loop first needs to propose a non-mass-action (saturating) rate law and
fit its parameters (Km, Vmax). The parsimony evaluator decides between the forms
given what is observed. Builds on the scoring calibrated in recover-mass-action.
investigations.title: Recover enzyme kinetics (Michaelis-Menten)
investigations.objective:
From synthetic data generated by a known enzyme-kinetics model, can the cycle
recover a flat SBML — and does it recover the elementary mechanism
(E + S <-> ES -> E + P) or the reduced Michaelis-Menten rate law, and which is
the parsimonious answer the data actually support?

investigations.name: recover-gene-switch
investigations.description:
Third rung — the first with genuine nonlinearity and multistability. Ground truth
is a Hill-repression switch with two stable steady states; synthetic targets
include trajectories from initial conditions in both basins. The data
underdetermine the mechanism, so this rung stresses frontier-driven refinement:
the discovery cycle must use the residual (unexplained branch / sharpness) to
propose the Hill nonlinearity rather than fit a linear surrogate. Exercises the
reaction-proposer and rate-law-fitter on a non-mass-action regulatory term.
investigations.title: Recover a Hill gene switch
investigations.objective:
From synthetic data of a bistable Hill-repression gene switch, can the cycle
recover a flat SBML that reproduces both stable branches and the nonlinear
(Hill) regulation — a case where the data alone underdetermine the mechanism?

investigations.name: recover-mass-action
investigations.description:
Baseline rung of the recovery ladder. The ground truth is a small mass-action
network (A -> B with rate k1; A + B <-> C with k2/k2r). A synthetic-target
generator simulates it (tellurium) to produce the observed species trajectories;
only those trajectories + the species list are exposed to the loop. The
discovery-engine cycle proposes candidate reactions, simulates, compares to the
target, and refines until acceptance. Because the oracle is known, structural
recovery and parsimony are gradeable exactly. This study calibrates the
trajectory-comparator and structural-scorer capabilities before the harder rungs.
investigations.title: Recover mass-action kinetics
investigations.objective:
Given only synthetic time-series generated from a known mass-action SBML model
(A -> B, reversible binding A + B <-> C), can the discovery-engine cycle rebuild
a flat SBML that reproduces the trajectories and recovers the actual reactions
and rate constants?

investigations.name: recover-oscillator
investigations.description:
Fourth and hardest rung. Ground truth is a limit-cycle oscillator (e.g.
repressilator — three-gene cyclic repression — or the Brusselator). Synthetic
targets are multi-period trajectories. The recovered model must reproduce the
oscillation as a stable limit cycle, so trajectory scoring is phase-aware and the
structural score targets the feedback loop. This rung most sharply tests the
reaction-proposer and rate-law-fitter, and is the natural trigger for the
non-recoverability detector if a faithful flat-SBML form proves out of reach.
investigations.title: Recover an oscillator
investigations.objective:
From synthetic data of a limit-cycle oscillator (repressilator or Brusselator),
can the cycle recover a flat SBML whose topology reproduces the oscillation —
period and amplitude — as sustained dynamics, not just a point-wise fit over one
window?

investigations.name: recover-stochastic-abm
investigations.description:
Adversarial / negative-control rung. The oracle is the SAME mass-action network as
recover-mass-action, but observed as one Gillespie trajectory at low copy numbers
(recover-stochastic-abm). Deterministically it is a flat reaction network; as a
single stochastic path it is not — its derivatives are dominated by shot noise. This
is the ABM/stochastic boundary the sbml-decomposition investigation found (an ABM
reduces to an SBML/ODE only in the large-population limit). The study is a control
for the whole ladder: the metric must pass by rejecting a system it should not claim
to recover, so the recovery capabilities are not just curve-fitting anything.
investigations.title: Reject a stochastic system (no flat-SBML form)
investigations.objective:
Does the recovery pipeline correctly REFUSE to recover a flat SBML from a single
low-copy stochastic trajectory — recognizing the ABM/stochastic boundary where no
deterministic flat-SBML reaction network faithfully fits the data?

investigations.name: bigger-models-and-abm-limit
investigations.description: Adversarial study merging the two boundary probes of the SBML-decomposition investigation. (1) SCALE: a synthetic N-organ body (species=3N+1, reactions=4N, all organs coupled through one shared blood pool) run as ONE Tellurium model (engine_monolithic, model=multiorgan_scaled) versus decomposed into N per-organ nodes sharing a blood store. (2) ABM LIMIT: a well-mixed stochastic Lotka-Volterra ABM (predator_prey_abm, exact Gillespie SSA over integer populations) versus its deterministic mean-field ODE in libroadrunner/CVODE (predator_prey_meanfield), at a large (K=400) and a small (K=8) population scale.
investigations.title: Bigger models and the ABM limit (adversarial)
investigations.objective: Where do the SBML/Tellurium assumptions stop holding: (a) as an SBML model grows to hundreds-to-thousands of species, where does a monolithic libroadrunner/CVODE instance strain, and does decomposing it come out ahead end-to-end; (b) can an agent-based model even BE an SBML/Tellurium model, and where does its mean-field ODE reduction hold and structurally break?
investigations.claim: The one strong, well-measured result is that the MONOLITHIC libroadrunner BUILD strains superlinearly in the reaction count: 0.20 s at 97 species -> 1.76 s at 385 -> 5.54 s at 769 -> 18.5 s at 1537 species (~94x for ~16x the reactions, ~O(N^1.64)), with the dense-CVODE run blowing up alongside it (0.0023 s -> 2.56 s). That is the real strain point and the reason a very large SBML model is painful to run monolithically. Decomposition is NOT a free win: building N small models is SLOWER than the single compile up to ~100 species (1.7x slower at 97 species), reaches only rough parity at 385 species (1.40 vs 1.76 s) and becomes a clear build win only at ~1500 species (2.4x); and the decomposed per-tick RUN overhead is ~16x the monolith's CVODE run, so the decomposed body is SLOWER END-TO-END at every N measured (decomp_total 2.35 s vs mono_total 1.81 s at 385 species). The end-to-end gap narrows with N but the decomposed run is unmeasured past N=128, so no end-to-end crossover is claimed. Decomposition is a structural trade — it swaps the monolith's superlinear build for much higher run overhead — that would only pay off end-to-end on models larger than measured. CRUCIAL caveat: the additive-split accuracy is good only at small N / fine interval (max_rel_err 2e-3 at N=2, 1.2e-2 at N=8, 5.2e-2 at N=32) and is 0.31 (31%) at N=128 — so the regime where the speed gap narrows and the regime of acceptable accuracy do NOT co-occur at a fixed coupling interval. All numbers measured, not fabricated. ALSO: An agent-based model reduces to an SBML/Tellurium mean-field ODE ONLY in the large-population, well-mixed, deterministic limit; it structurally cannot capture stochasticity, discreteness, extinction, or individual heterogeneity. MEASURED (Lotka-Volterra, base rates r=a=b=m=1, start density (1.8, 1.0), horizon ~2 periods, seed 0): at a LARGE population scale K=400 (80 SSA runs) the mean-field ODE reproduces the SSA ensemble mean to a max relative error of 4.9% with 0% of runs seeing predator or total extinction — the reduction is VALID. At a SMALL scale K=8 (200 SSA runs) the stochastic system collapses: the PREDATORS go extinct in 86.5% of runs and BOTH species in 51.0%, hitting absorbing states that the neutrally-stable ODE — which simply orbits forever, 0% extinction of either species at any K — can never reach, and the ensemble mean diverges several-fold from the ODE (predator-extinct runs let the prey escape, so the mean no longer resembles the bounded ODE cycle). The ODE additionally cannot represent the ensemble variance at ANY K. So "can an ABM be an SBML model?" has an honest, quantified answer: yes, but only as its large-population mean-field limit, and that reduction silently discards exactly the stochastic/discrete phenomena (extinction, demographic noise) that are often the biological point. This breaks the naive "just write it as SBML" claim.

investigations.name: biological-modular-seam
investigations.description: Study in the SBML-decomposition investigation on Teusink glycolysis (BIOMD0000000064, 17 floating species). The model is authored as inline Antimony and shown in the Model tab. Two SubmodelProcess nodes (upper/lower glycolysis) + an EnergyStep share ONE species store and reconcile additive deltas through the real bigraph apply/reconcile path. Realised by the generic reaction_split composite (seam=aldolase, tellurium + tellurium).
investigations.title: Biological seam: modular submodels
investigations.objective: If the model is partitioned along a biological seam (upper vs lower glycolysis at aldolase/F16P) into two coupled process nodes sharing a store, does it still reproduce the reference, and is this a genuine multi-process composition?
investigations.claim: A biological-seam decomposition reproduces the reference (0.468 → 0.100 as the coupling step shrinks, T=0.15) as a GENUINE multi-process composition — the first point on the spectrum where the model is composable.

investigations.name: cross-engine-coupling
investigations.description: Study in the SBML-decomposition investigation on Teusink glycolysis (BIOMD0000000064, 17 floating species). The model is authored as inline Antimony and shown in the Model tab. cross-engine-coupling swaps biological-modular-seam's lower-glycolysis submodel for the native-pbg process while upper stays libroadrunner, both sharing one store. This is the composability existence proof; it has no monolithic reference (accuracy-exempt). The generic reaction_split composite makes the engine a parameter of each side of the seam: the baseline couples Tellurium (upper) with COPASI (lower); the native-lower variant couples Tellurium with the hand-ported native process. Both reproduce the Tellurium+Tellurium biological-seam result at the same coupling interval to ~3e-7 (measured below).
investigations.title: Cross-engine coupling: engines are interchangeable at a seam
investigations.objective: Can one composite run part of the model in one engine and part in another (libroadrunner, COPASI, or the native process), sharing one store - a composition a monolithic SBML model structurally cannot express - and are the engines interchangeable at the seam?
investigations.claim: A single composite runs HALF in one engine and HALF in another, sharing one store - structurally impossible for a monolith. Swapping the lower half of the seam=aldolase composite from Tellurium to COPASI or to the native process reproduces the Tellurium+Tellurium trajectory at the same coupling interval (0.005) to max relative error 3.2e-7 (COPASI 3.19e-7, native 3.20e-7, measured); the engines are interchangeable at a seam as a ~1e-7 drop-in (COPASI is not bit-reproducible run to run). This is the composability payoff, not a numeric result.

investigations.name: decomposition-synthesis
investigations.description: The synthesis node of the SBML-decomposition investigation. It builds-on all seven arm studies, carrying each arm's results forward as inputs (RFC-0006 provides/outputs_used), and renders the investigation-wide comparison: the composability scorecard, the runtime + overhead breakdowns, the accuracy divergence, the speed-accuracy-composability tradeoff map, and the decision table. These are investigation-scope views (every one spans 4-6 arms) and live here rather than under any single arm, where they would read as being about that one arm.
investigations.title: Decomposition synthesis — the cross-arm landscape
investigations.objective: Across all seven decomposition strategies, what is the speed x accuracy x composability landscape, and which strategy wins for which regime?
investigations.claim: The seven arms span a speed-accuracy-composability frontier with no dominant point; the tradeoff map + decision table turn that frontier into a regime-specific recommendation.

investigations.name: ensemble-and-multirate
investigations.description: Methods study of the SBML-decomposition investigation on Teusink glycolysis (BIOMD0000000064, 17 floating species), merging two ensemble questions on the generic ensemble composite. SAME-RATE (intervals unset): N monolithic Tellurium instances run concurrently via Ray OS processes with parameter draws. MULTI-RATE (intervals=geometric): N independent monolithic instances, each advanced on a different geometrically-spaced interval, run under scheduler=scan (stock O(P^2) tick loop) and scheduler=heap (#270 event-heap, O(P log P)); the instances share no store and are uncoupled, so there is no splitting error and only the scheduler changes.
investigations.title: Ensemble throughput and multi-rate scheduling
investigations.objective: When many instances of the monolithic model are run together, (a) as a same-rate parameter ensemble does vivarium orchestration on a real parallel backend (Ray) deliver a genuine throughput speedup, and (b) as a genuinely multi-rate ensemble (each instance on a different interval) does process-bigraph #270's event-heap scheduler beat the stock scan loop as the process count grows, while staying bit-identical?
investigations.claim: A Ray ensemble of monoliths gives a real 7.5x wall-clock speedup on 16 cores — the one study where vivarium wins on speed; libroadrunner does NOT release the GIL, so in-process threads cannot (they backfire). Separately, process-bigraph #270's event-heap scheduler is bit-identical to the stock scan loop (same math, different tick order) and its wall-clock advantage grows monotonically with P on a genuinely multi-rate composite — measured 0.98x at P=4 (heap bookkeeping with nothing to gain), crossing over near P~50-64, to 1.64x at P=256 on real libroadrunner/CVODE instances. The per-process CVODE integration dominates the per-tick scan until P reaches the low hundreds, so the multiplier is modest at the P a unit test can afford; it is reported as measured, and the regime where it grows large (hundreds-to-thousands of cheap processes) is #270's own 4.8x@P=100 -> 46x@P=1000 micro-benchmark, cited not reproduced.

investigations.name: fully-native-pbg
investigations.description: Study in the SBML-decomposition investigation on Teusink glycolysis (BIOMD0000000064, 17 floating species). The model is authored as inline Antimony and shown in the Model tab. The 17 Teusink rate laws + the 3 sqrt assignment rules are hand-ported to pure Python/numpy and integrated with scipy LSODA — no libroadrunner at runtime. Built in two leaf variants (scalar-dict and numpy-array). Realised by the generic native_composite (model=glycolysis).
investigations.title: Fully native process-bigraph
investigations.objective: Can the glycolysis ODE network be reimplemented as native process-bigraph processes (no libroadrunner at runtime) at reference fidelity, and does the state leaf representation (scalar-dict vs numpy-array) matter for performance at this scale?
investigations.claim: A fully native process-bigraph implementation reaches reference fidelity (~1e-7); at 17 species the scalar-dict-vs-array leaf choice is perf-irrelevant (only bites at 100s-1000s of species).

investigations.name: mechanical-split-cost
investigations.description: Methods study of the SBML-decomposition investigation on Teusink glycolysis (BIOMD0000000064, 17 floating species). The model is authored as inline Antimony and shown in the Model tab. A MECHANICAL split (not a biological seam): the reactions are partitioned into complementary groups in two Tellurium process nodes that share one species store and reconcile ADDITIVELY (Jacobi: both groups advance from the same state each coupling interval and their deltas sum). Because both groups advance from the same state, the splitting error is first order in the coupling interval and is measured here against the monolithic Tellurium reference on this additive composite (max relative error 0.857 at interval 0.1, 0.112 at 0.0125, 0.0066 at 0.001).
investigations.title: Mechanical split: the cost of splitting
investigations.objective: If the same model is split mechanically (not along a biological seam) into two reaction groups that exchange state through ONE shared additive store each coupling interval, how much orchestration overhead and splitting error does that add, and does the error shrink with the interval?
investigations.claim: Mechanical-split (additive-coupling) error is real and shrinks monotonically with the coupling interval (max relative error 0.857 at 0.1 → 0.112 at 0.0125 → 0.0066 at 0.001, measured against the monolithic reference); a clean split was only possible across the weakly-coupled glycogen/trehalose sinks — splitting across the strong P/ATP/ADP energy coupling diverges.

investigations.name: sbml-in-tellurium
investigations.description: Study in the SBML-decomposition investigation on Teusink glycolysis (BIOMD0000000064, 17 floating species). The model is authored as inline Antimony and shown in the Model tab. sbml-in-tellurium hands the entire model to libroadrunner/CVODE in one piece — fast, numerically exact, but opaque and uncomposable. Realised by the generic engine_monolithic composite (model=glycolysis, engine=tellurium).
investigations.title: Monolithic Tellurium (reference)
investigations.objective: Does the whole SBML model, integrated in one libroadrunner/CVODE call through a single TelluriumProcess, reproduce the model's reference trajectory, and what is its performance baseline?
investigations.claim: Monolithic Tellurium reproduces the reference to ~1e-6 and is the fastest approach — the speed + accuracy reference.
